# Title is here

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: true

library(reticulate)
source("R/functions.R")
# Imported function demo
result <- calculate_growth(150, 100)
print(paste("The growth rate is", result, "%"))

# R Dataframe
r_data <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  measurement = c(10.2, 11.5, 10.8, 12.1, 11.2)
)

print("Data created in R:")
print(r_data)



```

1. From R to Python
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Same data in python
df_in_python = r.r_data

print("Python sees the R data as a Pandas DataFrame:")
print(df_in_python.describe())

# Let's create a new column in Python
df_in_python['log_measurement'] = df_in_python['measurement'].apply(lambda x: x**2)
```

1. From Python to R Change here
```{r}
# Access the Python object using 'py$variable_name'
final_r_data <- py$df_in_python

print("R now has the data modified by Python:")
View(final_r_data) # Opens in vscode spreadsheat

```


```{r}
# Load ggplot2 (install it first if you haven't: install.packages("ggplot2"))
library(ggplot2)


# Using the built-in 'economics' dataset for a forecast-style look
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2c3e50", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Testing Internal R Graphics",
    subtitle = "If this is in VS Code, we have achieved total success.",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Unemployment (thousands)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
# Plots in new window
```

```{r}
# Install it once: install.packages("plotly")
library(plotly) # Same plotly as in python -> interactive in vscode
library(ggplot2)

# Create a ggplot
p <- ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) + geom_line()

# Use ggplotly to "View" it inside VS Code
ggplotly(p)
```
